intro.author: Ezekiel son of Buzi, a priest carried to Babylon with King Jehoiachin in 597 BC (1:1-3)
intro.written: Prophecies dated from about 593 to 571 BC, given in Babylonia
intro.audience: Judean exiles living in Babylonia, and through them the people still in Jerusalem
intro.setting: Ezekiel lived among exiles at Tel-abib by the river Chebar, a canal in southern Babylonia. For six years he warned that Jerusalem would fall despite hopes of a quick return; after news of its destruction arrived in 586 BC, his message turned to restoration.
intro.purpose: To explain why God let Jerusalem and the temple fall, to call the exiles to personal repentance, and to promise that God would cleanse, revive and dwell again with his people.
intro.bigIdea: The glory that left the defiled temple will return, so that all will 'know that I am the LORD.'

outline.title: Restoration: new heart, new life, a shepherd-king
Vision of a new temple and a renewed land

commentary.t: THE BOOK OF THE PROPHET EZEKIEL
